To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose to dynamically adapt exploration in multi-agent reinforcement learning using a multi-armed bandits to optimize a proxy for learning progress and that we demonstrate the approach on a suite of 57 Atari 2600 environments, showing that our method is competitive with per-task tuning at the cost of a single bandit.

(1) a multi-armed bandits can be used to dynamically adapt the exploration strategy in reinforcement learning, (2) the exploration can be controlled by modulating multiple policy parameters in an efficient way and (3) the approach produces results comparable with the state of the art at a fraction of computational cost.

(a) the proposed method is a simple yet effective approach to adapt exploration to the task and (b) the method outperforms the state-of-the-art in terms of sample efficiency and robustness to task difficulty.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to generate experience to best facilitate learning in multi-task reinforcement learning.
the problem of how to best adapt the data generation to the task and the learner, in order to optimize the learning process.
the question of how to best generate experience for learning in multi-agent systems.

this paper presents an interesting approach to adapt exploration for learning, but that there is a lot of work to do before the method is ready to be used on real-world tasks.
we propose a novel method for learning to adapt exploration, and demonstrate that it can be used to learn a good policy in a wide variety of Atari games.
this work demonstrates a general framework to adapt behaviour for learning progress in a distributed setting.

we propose a new method to control the exploration of a multi-agent system.
we have developed a new approach for exploration in multi-task reinforcement learning that is more flexible and efficient than prior work.
the proposed approach can be used as an effective tool for balancing exploration and exploitation in reinforcement learning.

the data distribution can be adapted in an efficient manner to improve the learning progress of the underlying learning algorithm.
it is possible to learn how to adapt the learning process in order to maximize learning progress, which is an important step in the direction of general reinforcement learning agents.
the data generation process should be considered as an integral part of the agent's learning process, and that it is feasible to adapt the exploration strategy to optimize learning progress.
